title: Dart
subtitle: The language behind Flutter: sound null safety, records and patterns, sealed classes, async code and isolates, from a first program to a finished project.
description: Dart is a general-purpose, garbage-collected language that Google announced in 2011. It is best known as the language of Flutter, the toolkit used to build apps for Android, iOS, the web and desktop from one codebase, but it is also a capable language on its own for command-line tools and servers. Dart compiles ahead of time to native machine code, to JavaScript and to WebAssembly, and runs on a fast virtual machine with hot reload during development. Its type system is sound, and since Dart 3 every program is null safe.

This course is for anyone who knows what a variable, a loop and a function are, for example from the [Start level of Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience. It covers the language itself rather than Flutter: variables and sound null safety, control flow and functions, collections, classes, mixins and extensions, the records, patterns and sealed classes of Dart 3, futures, streams and isolates, and the tools professionals use for packages, analysis and testing. Flutter's widget model is described in the last lesson, which ends with a complete project.

To run the code, install the Dart SDK from [dart.dev/get-dart](https://dart.dev/get-dart) (the Flutter SDK includes it too), or paste any program into [DartPad](https://dartpad.dev/), the official online playground, which runs Dart in your browser. Every complete program in these lessons was run with `dart run` on Dart 3.14, and its output is shown exactly as it printed.
